sampling_method: Every own-result cell in frame_locations was assigned a contiguous 1-based index in reading order (location order below; row-major within a table, walking each row top-to-bottom in its printed order and left-to-right across that row's own-result columns only, skipping baseline/hyperparameter columns in between), giving a population of 1..330. Two caption-wide ownership rules recur and are applied per cell, not per row: (1) wherever a table's caption states the authors themselves ran an evaluation for every row shown -- Table 2's 'we run the k-NN evaluation for models with official released weights', or Tables 7/13/14/15 and the Appendix E multi-crop-frameworks table's 'run for N epochs'/'run by us' ablations -- that column (or whole table) is own-result even on rows named for a prior method (BYOL, MoCo-v2, SwAV), while an un-asterisked accuracy/Linear column on the same row not covered by such a blanket statement stays a citation baseline; (2) speed/throughput/memory figures (im/s, im/sec, time, mem.) are results per this file's rules and are own wherever the surrounding caption attributes the measurement to the authors, which happens uniformly in this paper (Table 1, Table 2, Table 8, Appendix D's heads ablation) -- each printed instance is counted separately even when the digits repeat because several rows share one architecture (e.g. im/s=1237 on every RN50 row of Table 2). Architecture-spec columns (#params, dim, blocks, heads, #tokens) are hyperparameter, not result, and excluded throughout, matching convnext.json's GFLOPs exclusion. A delta stated in prose without its constituent absolutes restated in the same passage is counted as its own cell (e.g. Section 4.1's '+3.5% with linear classification', Table 5's '+9.1% (J&F)m'); a delta whose absolutes are printed beside it in the same sentence, or that is pure arithmetic over values already given earlier in the same paragraph, is excluded to avoid double-counting (e.g. Section 5.4's '+2% while requiring 2x less time' immediately after the 72.5/74.6% and 46h/24h absolutes). Ranges ('+1-2%') are excluded per the labelling rules. random.seed(20260810); random.sample(range(1, 331), 15) drew {1, 3, 25, 28, 49, 57, 139, 166, 182, 197, 214, 216, 244, 295, 305}; each label below records its draw as frame_index.
